zh: 我们深入这些公司的程度有多深,以及我们如何把它们改得更好,至少这是我们努力实现的目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those transformations take a lot of time and effort.
zh: 这些转型需要大量的时间和精力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we find that that time and that effort do not scale linearly with the revenue potential of those businesses.
zh: 而我们发现,这些时间和精力并不会随着这些业务的收入潜力线性扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: In other words, we don't need nearly as many people.
zh: 换句话说,我们不需要接近那么多的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or let me phrase it differently.
zh: 或者换一种说法。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can get it done for a much larger business with a relatively similar number of people as for a smaller business.
zh: 对于一个规模大得多的业务,我们可以用和较小业务相对相近的人数把它搞定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so given that we don't have infinite operational capacity, we prefer to acquire, I don't know, five or 10 businesses each year, but bigger than 50 smaller ones.
zh: 因此,鉴于我们的运营能力不是无限的,我们更倾向于每年收购,我不知道,五到十家业务,但规模更大,而不是五十家更小的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's been our approach, hence the increase in the average scale of the businesses as opposed to the frequency of the acquisitions to make sure we keep compounding revenue very rapidly.
zh: 所以这一直是我们的方式,因此业务的平均规模在增加,而不是收购频率,以确保我们能让收入持续快速复利增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: How big can it get?
zh: 那能大到什么程度?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, so far, we see no end in sight.
zh: 嗯,到目前为止,我们看不到尽头。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is no obvious saturation point.
zh: 没有明显的饱和点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's very difficult to tell if and when growth will slow down.
zh: 我是说,很难判断增长是否、何时会放缓。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sure it'll slow down at some point.
zh: 我确信在某个时候它会放缓。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm having some issues with Google.
zh: 我在 Google 上遇到了一些麻烦。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know if that's of interest for you.
zh: 我不知道这是否是你感兴趣的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, maybe in the future.
zh: 嗯,也许是未来的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's pretty far away.
zh: 我觉得那还挺遥远的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have joked, I mean, look, just jokingly.
zh: 我们开玩笑说过,我是说,只是开个玩笑。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we have sometimes joked maybe one day.
zh: 我是说,我们有时会开玩笑说,也许有一天。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, who knows?
zh: 你知道的,谁知道呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of the AOL...
zh: 一些 AOL……

speaker: Unknown
en: At some point was, broadly speaking, as prominent and dominant as Google has been in the past decade.
zh: 在某个时期,广义上讲,和过去十年的 Google 一样显赫和占主导地位。

speaker: Unknown
en: So maybe in 20 years, but I actually like Google a lot.
zh: 所以也许是 20 年后的事,不过我其实很喜欢 Google。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hope they do super well and we do super well.
zh: 我希望他们做得超级好,我们也做得超级好。

speaker: Unknown
en: You guys operate very efficiently per employee.
zh: 你们的人均运营效率非常高。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the last metric you mentioned was $4 million in revenue per employee.
zh: 我记得你提到的最后一个指标是每位员工 400 万美元的收入。

speaker: Unknown
en: Per Spooner, which is a member of that core team now approaching 1,000 people.
zh: 每 per Spooner,也就是那个核心团队的成员,目前接近 1000 人。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you count everybody we have on board, including acquired teams, it's probably a little less than half of it.
zh: 如果算上我们所有的在编人员,包括被收购的团队,大概是这个数字的一半略少一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's still very high, but a little bit less than half that number probably.
zh: 仍然非常高,但大概是那个数字的一半略少一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: But because you know how efficiently and lean you can run a company, do you just look at all these big tech companies, all these other companies out there, and are you just like, what are you guys doing?
zh: 但因为你深知一家公司可以运营得多高效、多精简,你会不会看着所有这些大型科技公司、所有这些其他公司,然后心想,你们在干什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you make of that?
zh: 你怎么看待这件事?

speaker: Unknown
en: No, I mean, we don't have, it's very easy to criticize from the outside, you know, it's quite difficult to run a business, we know firsthand, and a lot of the ways we manage to create value relative to the previous owners are not available to those owners and those management teams under their particular circumstances.
zh: 不,我是说,我们并不……从外部批评是很容易的,你知道,经营一家企业是相当难的,我们有切身体会,而且我们相对于前任所有者创造价值的许多方式,在他们的特定处境下,是那些所有者和管理团队无法采用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, again, a big part of our value creation comes from that set of proprietary technologies.
zh: 比如说,再举一次,我们价值创造很大一部分来自那套专有技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: We discussed it.
zh: 我们讨论过。

speaker: Unknown
en: It would be uneconomical, unrealistic for those businesses to build them, so they don't have them.
zh: 对于那些业务来说,自建这些东西是不经济、不现实的,所以他们没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many times, businesses attract very good talent during their heyday, and then as they are still pretty nice businesses, maybe growing, but a little bit more, you know, their opportunity has been saturated a little bit more.
zh: 很多时候,业务在鼎盛时期能吸引到非常优秀的人才,然后随着它们仍然是相当不错的业务,也许还在增长,但你知道,机会已经更加饱和了一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're not as cool any longer.
zh: 它们不再那么酷了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They stop attracting some of the strongest talent.
zh: 它们停止吸引一些最强的人才。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of the people who are most entrepreneurial-driven, proactive start moving on to other businesses.
zh: 一些最具创业精神、最有主动性的人开始转向其他业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so those management teams find themselves occasionally having to, or more often than not really, actually, having to run those businesses with perfectly fine talent, but not like...
zh: 于是那些管理团队发现自己时不时地——或者实际上,更多时候是真的——不得不用还算合格的人才来运营那些业务,但不是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Top-notch talent in many cases.
zh: 在很多情况下,不是顶尖的人才。

speaker: Unknown
en: At Venice Rooms, we have been able to attract, I think, extremely strong talent.
zh: 在 Venice Rooms,我们吸引到了,我认为,极其强的人才。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had 800,000 job applications in 2025.
zh: 我们在 2025 年收到了 80 万份工作申请。

speaker: Unknown
en: We hired 300,000 people.
zh: 我们雇了 30 万人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we can introduce, add to those teams selectively.
zh: 所以我们可以选择性地向这些团队引入、增加人员。

speaker: Unknown
en: Individuals who are extremely high performance, extremely high agency, very competent in relevant areas.
zh: 引入那些极其高绩效、主观能动性极强、在相关领域非常胜任的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that fuels a new wave of innovations, of efficiency.
zh: 这就推动了一波新的创新和效率提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, that's not a shortcoming of the previous executive team.
zh: 再说一次，这不是之前高管团队的缺点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just they didn't have the employer brand.
zh: 只是他们没有雇主品牌

speaker: Unknown
en: attract those people.
zh: 来吸引那些人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of those people join BennySpoons because they like the idea that they can rotate over time over multiple businesses and platform teams that enables tremendous growth and it keeps it interesting and a lot of career opportunities.
zh: 很多这些人加入 BennySpoons 是因为他们喜欢这样一个理念：他们可以随着时间在多个业务和平台团队之间轮岗，这带来了巨大的成长，也让工作保持有趣，还有很多职业机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that employer brand can only exist if you structure your company like BennySpoons.
zh: 所以这种雇主品牌只有在你把公司构造成像 BennySpoons 这样时才可能存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can never achieve it as a, say, single product company.
zh: 作为一家，比如说，单一产品公司，你永远做不到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's to say a second major difference that drives performance and that's not available for those teams.
zh: 那就是说，这是第二个推动绩效的重大差异，而那些团队没有这个优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: A third one could be different incentives.
zh: 第三个可能是不同的激励。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're running a business and it's just one product, the markets will typically almost primarily value you based on your organic growth.
zh: 如果你经营一项业务，而它只是一个产品，市场通常会几乎主要以你的有机增长来给你估值。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is your subscriber count growing?
zh: 你的订阅用户数在增长吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is your revenue growing?
zh: 你的收入在增长吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: How fast?
zh: 增长多快？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if you're invested in a company, really the upside is in believing that that company grows.
zh: 因为如果你投资了一家公司，真正的上行空间在于相信那家公司会增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's still value in a flatter company, but there's not a lot of discussion there.
zh: 一家增长平缓的公司仍然有价值，但没有太多可讨论的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not as exciting.
zh: 不那么令人兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: Multiples compress.
zh: 倍数会被压缩。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's this pressure for management teams to show growth at all costs.
zh: 所以管理层团队面临这种不惜一切代价展示增长的压力。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you only have one product or, let's say,
zh: 但如果你只有一个产品，或者说，

speaker: Unknown
en: set of products in a niche in the market.
zh: 市场中某个利基市场里的一组产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes there's not a lot you can do to ignite a lot of growth because maybe that market has been saturated.
zh: 有时你没有太多办法去点燃大量增长，因为也许那个市场已经饱和了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The truly big groundbreaking ideas have been had and having whatever missing one is out there in the universe of possibilities is difficult.
zh: 真正重大的突破性想法都已经被想过了，而在所有可能性中找出那个缺失的想法是很难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so sometimes people throw a lot of money, whether it's R&D or marketing, just desperately trying to
zh: 所以有时人们投入大量资金，无论是研发还是营销，只是拼命 trying to

speaker: Unknown
en: to unlock that extra growth and that improved multiple.
zh: 解锁那额外的增长和那改善的倍数。

speaker: Unknown
en: If that business becomes part of Bending Spoons, we still really like to make it grow, of course, as much as we can, but there is no pressure to grow beyond what's profitable growth.
zh: 如果那项业务成为 Bending Spoons 的一部分，我们当然仍然非常希望让它增长，尽我们所能，但没有超出可盈利增长范围的增长压力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because ultimately anybody who buys stock into Bending Spoons, yes, they like our individual businesses to do well, of course, but the main thesis is Bending Spoons can generate amazing cash flows from businesses and redeploy toward new acquisitions at very high returns and this over time compounds attractively, hopefully for many, many years.
zh: 因为归根结底，任何买入 Bending Spoons 股票的人，是的，他们当然希望我们的各个业务表现良好，但主要的论点是 Bending Spoons 能够从业务中产生惊人的现金流，并以非常高的回报重新部署到新的收购上，而这随时间复利增长，颇具吸引力，希望持续很多很多年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so do I care all that much whether
zh: 所以我是否真的那么在意

speaker: Unknown
en: You know that particular business is growing 15% or 5%?
zh: 你知道，那项特定的业务是增长 15% 还是 5%？

speaker: Unknown
en: Not really.
zh: 并不真的在意。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean I'd like to know and 15 is better than 5 but if 15 is achieved by burning a lot of cash for very little...
zh: 我是说我想知道，而且 15 比 5 好，但如果 15 是通过烧掉大量现金、却只换来很少的……

speaker: Unknown
en: A profit many years into the future, I'd rather get five and have all that extra cash being deployed toward acquisitions that are accredited.
zh: 未来多年的一点利润换来的，我宁愿要 5%，把所有那些额外的现金部署到那些有增益的收购上。

speaker: Unknown
en: So often these executive teams and those owners are extremely competent, otherwise they probably wouldn't have built successful businesses.
zh: 所以这些高管团队和那些所有者往往极其胜任，否则他们可能也建不成成功的业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: The very structure and context in which they operate puts them at a disadvantage vis-a-vis that business being run within managements.
zh: 正是他们所处的结构和环境，让他们相对于在 managements 内部运营的那项业务处于劣势。

speaker: Unknown
en: One thing that I learned through all this is not only are the products super retentive and people might think that, oh, you might be buying this product, you'll be ruthlessly cutting headcount, you'll be making it more expensive, maybe you'll have churn, but no, retention's still good.
zh: 我从这一切中学到的一件事是，不仅这些产品留存率超高——人们可能会想，哦，你买下这个产品后，你会无情地裁减人手，你会让它更贵，也许会出现流失——但不，留存率依然很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also within this type of organization where you, if you have really high agency, if you have really good ownership in yourself and you can kind of move around, you're...
zh: 而且在这种类型的组织里，如果你有真正高的主观能动性，如果你对自己有真正好的主人翁意识，你可以四处走动，你……

speaker: Unknown
en: You're giving a lot of that to your employees and they're really retentive too.
zh: 你把很多这样的东西给了你的员工，他们的留存率也非常高。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you've created two really high quality kind of systems here.
zh: 所以你在这里创造了两个非常高质量的体系。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think it's a good way of looking at it.
zh: 是的，我觉得这是一种很好的看待方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have businesses with lower retention, businesses with higher retention, but I can't recall a single instance where retention got worse after Benny Spoons took over.
zh: 我们有留存率较低的业务，也有留存率较高的业务，但我想不起来有任何一例在 Benny Spoons 接手后留存率变差的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: Often it's improved, it's at least stayed the same, but ultimately we win by being relatively better.
zh: 通常它是提升了，至少保持不变，但归根结底，我们靠相对更好来获胜。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't need to...
zh: 我们不需要……

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not that we necessarily need to buy only businesses with perfect retention as long as these businesses do better under us than under the previous owners.
zh: 并不是说我们必须只买留存率完美的业务，只要这些业务在我们手里比在前任所有者手里表现得更好就行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we bought businesses with mediocre retention and businesses with great retention and generally preserved or improved those retention rates.
zh: 所以我们买过留存率平平的业务，也买过留存率很好的业务，并且总体上保持或提升了那些留存率。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yes, when it comes to our team members, we are fanatical about creating one of the best work environments on the planet.
zh: 而是的，说到我们的团队成员，我们对于打造地球上最好的工作环境之一这件事是狂热的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think, you know, there's a lot we could improve and no doubt about it.
zh: 而且我认为，你知道，有很多我们可以改进的地方，这一点毫无疑问。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have plenty of flaws, but we've done pretty well there overall.
zh: 我们有不少缺点，但总体上我们在这方面做得相当好。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have had essentially no unwanted churn of...
zh: 我们基本上没有出现过不想要的人员流失……

speaker: Unknown
en: Spooners, these people, part of the core team.
zh: Spooners,这些人,是核心团队的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Last year we had 0.6%, so 0.6% were most companies in tech as far as I can tell.
zh: 去年是 0.6%,也就是 0.6%——据我所知,大多数科技公司的情况是这样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now 5% is considered actually pretty good.
zh: 现在 5% 被认为其实是相当不错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of that super high retention comes from the excitement of being able to learn and grow across all of these different challenges.
zh: 这种极高的留任率很大程度上来自于能够在这么多不同的挑战中学习和成长所带来的兴奋感。

speaker: Unknown
en: It keeps it fresh and interesting.
zh: 这让工作保持新鲜和有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas if you're working on, say, Evernote, maybe it was exciting the first couple of years, let's say our product manager, but then after a while...
zh: 而如果你在做的是,比如说,Evernote,也许头几年很令人兴奋,假设你是我们的产品经理,但过了一段时间……

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, refining and refining, note-taking, it can grow stale.
zh: 你知道,一遍又一遍地打磨笔记功能,它会变得陈旧。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what can you do?
zh: 但你能怎么办呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: You like the company, but ultimately you have to look for a different employer to take another step, learn something new.
zh: 你喜欢这家公司,但最终你不得不寻找另一个雇主,去迈出新的一步,学点新东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: At BeneSpoon, you just raise your hand and say, I feel I've exhausted my creativity and excitement.
zh: 而在 BeneSpoon,你只需要举手说:我觉得我已经耗尽了创造力和激情。

speaker: Unknown
en: For Evernote, what else can I do?
zh: 对于 Evernote,我还能做点别的什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: And we may put you on a...
zh: 而我们可能会把你调到……

speaker: Unknown
en: Platform team to build an internal technology.
zh: 平台团队去构建内部技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could move to AOL and trying to improve email UX, which is a completely different and fascinating challenge.
zh: 你可以转到 AOL 去尝试改进邮件的用户体验,这是一个完全不同而且引人入胜的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yes, we have been able to retain people very effectively when it comes to the retention of teams that come on board through acquisitions.
zh: 所以是的,在留任通过收购加入的团队方面,我们一直能够非常有效地留住人才。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was quite worried initially that...
zh: 一开始我相当担心……

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of people would feel disheartened because we got acquired.
zh: 很多人会因为被收购而感到沮丧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes this is perceived as a failure, even though it's not.
zh: 有时这会被视为一种失败,尽管并不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: It may be a success, meaning that you actually got a nice exit, but you may feel that you're not as important as the core central team.
zh: 它可能是一种成功,意味着你实际上得到了一个不错的退出,但你可能会觉得自己不如核心中心团队那么重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there too, there is a lot we can improve and we value these teams and we're trying to do better, but overall...
zh: 我认为在这方面也有很多我们可以改进的地方,我们重视这些团队,我们正在努力做得更好,但总体而言……

speaker: Unknown
en: I think things have gone a lot better than I thought they would.
zh: 我认为事情的发展比我预想的好得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have an excellent relationship with all team members.
zh: 我们与所有团队成员都保持着极佳的关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: Retention rates for those team members, in no case are they lower than pre-manicipants.
zh: 这些团队成员的留任率,在任何情况下都不低于收购前。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes they've improved substantially.
zh: 有时还大幅提升了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So at least we're not damaging the quality of those workplaces, if anything, in many cases improving it.
zh: 所以至少我们没有损害那些工作场所的质量,如果说有什么影响的话,很多情况下是在改善它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But those retention rates are not as high as those we have in the core team.
zh: 但那些留任率不如我们在核心团队的水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're more in line with what I said before that's considered okay for most technology companies.
zh: 它们更接近我之前所说的、对大多数科技公司来说算得上还可以的水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: What would you say is core to the culture here?
zh: 你认为这里文化的核心是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I mean, there are several things, but probably the one or two that truly stand out as particularly distinctive.
zh: 嗯,我是说,有几点,但可能真正突出、特别与众不同的一两点是——

speaker: Unknown
en: One is something called extreme ownership.
zh: 一个是叫做「极致主人翁精神」(extreme ownership)的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want everybody to care deeply, tremendously about being amazing at what they do, about helping their team and the company succeed.
